summary_setup: 2026-10-31, AWS us-east-1, c6a.4xlarge spot (AMD EPYC 7R13, 8 cores / 16 vCPUs, the CPU of the published runs), Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 7.0.0-1014-aws, GCC 13.3.0, CMake 3.28.3; avifenc 1.4.0, libaom 3.13.1, SVT-AV1 v4.2.0.

Images: the 99 size-range photos of the published c6a run (477.7 MP). Each timed run encodes them 3 times (297 files, 1,433 MP) at q60, `-y 420`, libaom `tune=iq`, SVT-AV1 `tune=3`, with `bench.py`'s own speed code (`bench.cpu_speed`, one timed pass).

Builds (exact flags in results.json `builds`): **stock** = the published build (CMake Release, `-O3`; SVT-AV1's `SVT_AV1_LTO` defaults to ON with GCC, so the published SVT-AV1 already had LTO). **tuned** = `-march=native` + LTO for all three: libaom via `AOM_EXTRA_C(XX)_FLAGS=-march=native` + CMake IPO (it has no option of its own), SVT-AV1 via its own `NATIVE=ON` and `SVT_AV1_LTO=ON`, libavif via `CMAKE_C(XX)_FLAGS` + IPO. **tuned + PGO** = tuned plus SVT-AV1's own `SVT_AV1_PGO`, trained with avifenc on the separate 100-image ~1 MP set (`bench/images`), never on the timing set.

Two instances. The **primary** host matched the published speeds (control below) and gives every number here unless marked. The first instance launched (**replica**) was 7-8 % slower at every encoder with the same bytes (no CPU steal or background load), so the same job ran on both; the replica also did the quality scoring, which is host-independent (it reproduced the published q60 bytes and scores exactly).
summary_findings: **Tuned builds (question a).** The published builds were CMake Release (`-O3`), and SVT-AV1 already had LTO. `-march=native` + LTO made libaom 3.3-3.5 % faster at speed 6 (0.8-2.2 % at speed 9) and SVT-AV1 1.4-4.5 % faster, depending on the preset. SVT-AV1's own PGO, trained on a different image set, gained the most: 11-13 % at presets 2-6 and 9-11 % at presets 8-9 over stock (two rounds on the primary host; 11-18 % on the replica). **Every tuned and PGO output is byte-identical to the stock output**, so the published BD-rates hold unchanged.

**Thread splits (question b).** Of the five encoders split (libaom speed 6 and 9, SVT-AV1 presets 4, 6 and 9), 16 × `-j 1` is the fastest or within noise of it for libaom speed 9 and SVT-AV1 presets 6 and 9. 8 × `-j 2` is faster for libaom speed 6 (+2.4 to +4.3 % over three comparisons) and SVT-AV1 preset 4 (+3.6 to +4.9 %), and about the same for preset 6 (+0.9 to +1.1 %). More threads per encode are slower everywhere: at 1 × `-j 16` libaom speed 6 runs 35 % slower and SVT-AV1 preset 9 84 % slower.

**Bytes across splits.** SVT-AV1 writes the same files at every split. libaom writes different files at any `-j` > 1 (the same files for 2, 4, 8 and 16 threads; all 99 images change at speed 6, 30 of 99 at speed 9). The compression is effectively the same: at q60, 0.11 % fewer bytes and 0.014 lower mean SSIMULACRA2 at speed 6; BD-rate +0.10 % at speed 6 and +0.00 % at speed 9 against the `-j 1` files.

**Best combinations measured** (primary host, against stock 16 × `-j 1`): SVT-AV1 preset 4 with PGO at 8 × `-j 2`: 17.9 MP/s vs 15.6 (+15 %). Preset 6 with PGO: 55.1-55.3 MP/s at 16 × `-j 1` and 55.5 at 8 × `-j 2`, vs 49.4 (+12 %). libaom speed 6, tuned, at 8 × `-j 2`: 31.1 vs 28.7 MP/s (+8 %).

**Tiling.** avifenc 1.4 tiles automatically when no tile option is given, so the published baselines (and every run here) used up to 8 tiles per image; `--autotiling` changes nothing. One tile per image runs at the same speed at 16 × `-j 1` (-0.7 to +1.6 %) and is 0.4-0.8 % smaller at equal SSIMULACRA2 (BD-rate median: libaom s6 -0.52 %, s9 -0.81 %; SVT-AV1 p4 -0.52 %, p6 -0.52 %, p9 -0.37 %). Comparisons between the CPU encoders move by at most ~0.3 point (both gain about the same); against an untiled libaom speed 6 anchor, a codec that does not tile would score about 0.5 point worse than against the published (tiled) anchor.
**Host variance.** One of the two c6a.4xlarge instances ran every encoder 7-8 % slower, with the same bytes; per-session controls are needed before comparing absolute speeds across sessions.
summary_notes: avifenc 1.4 tiles automatically by default (up to 8 tiles of at least 512 × 512 pixels, whatever `-j` is), so the published CPU baselines were tiled. One tile per image (`--tilerowslog2 0 --tilecolslog2 0`) runs at the same speed at 16 × `-j 1` and is about 0.5 % smaller at equal SSIMULACRA2 for both libaom and SVT-AV1 (sweeps above).

SVT-AV1 adds `-mno-avx` after `NATIVE`'s `-march=native`, so `NATIVE` does not let GCC auto-vectorise its generic C code with AVX2/FMA; its hand-written AVX2 kernels are used by every build (runtime dispatch). The CPU has no AVX-512.
libaom and libavif have no `-march=native`, LTO or PGO options of their own; no PGO build was made for libaom.
Not rebuilt in any build: libjpeg-turbo, libyuv, libpng, zlib (Ubuntu 24.04 packages).
Every run gave identical bytes in all three repeats of each image: all builds and splits are deterministic.

The replica host also drifted ~3 % slower during its session (libaom s6 26.7 at the start, 25.9 at the end), so its differences of a few per cent are less certain than the primary's (28.70 at the start, 28.61 at the end).
question: Reddit review by an SVT-AV1 developer: (a) were the CPU baselines built tuned? (b) is one avifenc -j 1 per vCPU the most efficient way to use the CPU?

instance.type: c6a.4xlarge (AMD EPYC 7R13, 8 cores / 16 vCPUs, SMT on, 32 MiB L3, 30 GiB)

hosts.primary: us-east-1d; stock speeds matched the published ones (libaom s6 28.70 vs 28.72 MP/s); every number in summary.md is from this host unless marked
hosts.replica: us-east-1c; the first instance launched. Same bytes as the published runs but 7-8 % slower at every encoder (no CPU steal, no background load, uniform clock); the identical job was run on it as a cross-host replication

environment.cpu: AMD EPYC 7R13 Processor, 16 logical CPUs, avx2 yes, fma yes, avx512f no; gcc -march=native resolves to znver3
environment.system_libraries: libjpeg-turbo 8 (libjpeg.so.8), libyuv, libpng, zlib from Ubuntu 24.04 in every build (not rebuilt)
environment.metric: ssimulacra2 from libjxl v0.11.1 (stock build, as in the published runs); decoding with the stock avifdec (libaom decoder)

images.set: bench/openimages_v4_gamut.csv via bench/fetch_images.py: all 100 downloaded with matching hashes this time; 9fba6f263f3c4f3e_tiny.jpg (346x519, the one the published c6a SVT-AV1 run lacked) was set aside so the set is exactly the published 99 images / 477.7 MP
images.speed_workload: bench.speed_set: the 99 images 3x = 297 encodes, 1433.0 MP per timed run (as published)
images.pgo_training: bench/images (bench/openimages_v4_validation_100.csv: 100 images, 78.7 MP), never used for timing

method.timing: bench.cpu_speed exactly as bench.py's CPU speed phase: q60, -y 420, --ignore-exif --ignore-xmp, libaom -s N -a tune=iq, SVT-AV1 -c svt -a preset=N -a tune=3; cpu_count // N avifenc -j N at once over the 297 files; one timed pass; MP/s = 1433.0 MP / wall time
method.splits: bench.py --avifenc-threads N (added in this branch): avifenc -j N with 16 // N encodes at once. libavif hands -j N to libaom as g_threads = N and to SVT-AV1 4.x as level_of_parallelism = N; SVT-AV1 4.2 accepts levels 1-6 and maps anything higher to 6 (with a warning), so -j 8 and -j 16 are both level 6 there
method.tiling: avifenc 1.4.0 enables automatic tiling whenever no tile option is given (apps/avifenc.c sets autoTiling = TRUE by default; the banner says 'automatic tiling'), and libavif 1.4.0 then uses up to 8 tiles of at least 512 x 512 pixels whatever -j is (src/write.c: threads = 8 passed to avifSetTileConfiguration). So the published runs and every run here except the 'no tiling' ones were tiled: 8 tiles for 56 of the 99 images (452 of 478 MP), 4 for 4, 2 for 33, 1 for 6. --autotiling is therefore a no-op (checked: same bytes); one tile per image needs --tilerowslog2 0 --tilecolslog2 0 (bench.py --no-tiling, added in this branch)
method.byte_identity: sha256 of every output; a run is 'identical' when all 99 images' outputs (first repeat) equal the stock -j 1 outputs; every run was also checked to give the same bytes in all 3 repeats of each image
method.quality: bench.encode_cpu_set + bench.score + bench.bd_rate (quality points 30,40,50,60,70,80) on the 99 images; BD-rate vs libaom speed 6 from bench/results/aws-g6-l4-gamut/results.json

stock.commands: the published setup: libaom: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DENABLE_TESTS=0 -DENABLE_DOCS=0 -DENABLE_EXAMPLES=0 -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=1; SVT-AV1: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF; libavif: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DAVIF_CODEC_AOM=SYSTEM -DAVIF_CODEC_SVT=SYSTEM -DAVIF_CODEC_DAV1D=OFF -DAVIF_BUILD_APPS=ON -DAVIF_LIBYUV=SYSTEM -DAVIF_LIBSHARPYUV=OFF -DAVIF_JPEG=SYSTEM -DAVIF_ZLIBPNG=SYSTEM
stock.libaom_effective: -O3 -DNDEBUG (CMake Release), no -march, no LTO; SIMD files get their own -msse2 ... -mavx2 and runtime CPU detection picks AVX2
stock.svt_effective: -O3 -DNDEBUG -fstack-protector-strong -mno-avx -flto=auto -fno-fat-lto-objects: SVT-AV1's SVT_AV1_LTO option defaults to ON with GCC >= 9, so the published stock build already had LTO (254 of 270 compile commands); SVT appends -mno-avx to all generic C code; ENABLE_AVX512 on (unused: no AVX-512 on this CPU); runtime dispatch picks AVX2

tuned.libaom: no -march or LTO option of its own (checked CMakeLists.txt / build/cmake): -DAOM_EXTRA_C_FLAGS=-march=native -DAOM_EXTRA_CXX_FLAGS=-march=native -DCMAKE_INTERPROCEDURAL_OPTIMIZATION=ON, on top of the stock options -> '-O3 -DNDEBUG ... -march=native -flto=auto -fno-fat-lto-objects' on 363 of 392 commands (the rest are yasm/link/other steps)
tuned.svt: its own options: -DNATIVE=ON -DSVT_AV1_LTO=ON (+ -DCMAKE_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY=<build>/Bin/ so it does not overwrite the stock build's binaries) -> '-march=native -fstack-protector-strong -mno-avx -O3 -DNDEBUG -flto=auto -fno-fat-lto-objects'. Note: SVT-AV1 adds -mno-avx after NATIVE's -march=native, so its generic C code gets znver3 tuning and the non-AVX extensions but no AVX/AVX2/FMA (the AVX2 kernels keep -mavx2)

pgo.svt: tuned options plus SVT-AV1's PGO support: -DSVT_AV1_PGO=ON -DSVT_AV1_PGO_DIR=<dir>, then the steps of its PGOCompileGen / PGOCompileUse targets run directly (cmake -DSVT_INTERNAL_PGO_GENERATE=ON -DSVT_INTERNAL_PGO_USE=OFF; cmake --build --clean-first --target SvtAv1EncApp; train; cmake -DSVT_INTERNAL_PGO_GENERATE=OFF -DSVT_INTERNAL_PGO_USE=ON; cmake --build --clean-first --target SvtAv1EncApp; install). The training replaces SVT's PGOGenerateProfile target, which encodes y4m video with SvtAv1EncApp --preset 2 --film-grain 8 --tune 0 and so does not exercise the still-image path
pgo.training: the instrumented libSvtAv1Enc via LD_LIBRARY_PATH under the tuned avifenc, on bench/images (100 images, 78.7 MP): presets 2, 4, 6, 8, 9 x q 30, 60, 80, tune=3, -y 420, 16 x -j 1 = 1500 encodes (142 s on the replica host, 130 s on the primary), 236 .gcda files; in the use build only the 12 safestringlib files (used by SvtAv1EncApp, not by the library's encode path) had no profile
pgo.libavif: as tuned, linked against opt-pgo's SVT-AV1 and opt-tuned's libaom (RUNPATH opt-pgo/lib:opt-tuned/lib, checked with ldd)

binary_sha256.note: libaom builds are bit-identical across the two hosts; SVT-AV1 libraries differ between hosts in every build (SVT embeds __DATE__/__TIME__ unless REPRODUCIBLE_BUILDS) but gave the same output bytes
